haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both produce the same status, body and headers. Only the 429 lockout differs, and it applies equally to unknown emails.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with the login page and "Too many attempts" message plus Retry-After. The password is not checked, and the failure is not recorded.
haiku-low.q3: If the login request carried a sid cookie, that old session is deleted in the same transaction that creates the new session.
haiku-low.q4: Only sid=<random 32-byte base64url ID>, with no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: Idle activity does not end it, but it stops working 12 hours after creation, since created_at is never updated and the absolute limit cannot be extended.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes that session row if present, clears the cookie with Max-Age=0, and redirects 302 to /login. With no usable cookie, it skips the SQL and does the same.
haiku-low.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the sessions row for sha256(sid), then replies 302 /login with the cookie cleared. A missing session deletes 0 rows, which is fine.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres sessions table, shared by both instances. Instances hold no state, so any instance looks up sha256 of the session ID.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, keyed by email with attempted_at. The database now() is compared with attempted_at to count failures in the last 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: It compares id_hash, last_seen_at within 30 minutes and created_at within 12 hours, using database now(). On a valid session it writes back last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 login page reading "Something went wrong. Please try again." The transaction rolls back, no session is issued, and the cookie is unchanged.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job every 10 minutes on each instance deletes sessions with last_seen_at older than 30 minutes or created_at older than 12 hours.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Unknown email and wrong password give the same status (401), body (login page "Invalid email or password") and headers.
sonnet.q2: It is locked out. The app returns 429 with the login page "Too many attempts. Please try again later." and a Retry-After header (seconds until locked_until). The password is never checked with bcrypt, and failures during the lock are not recorded.
sonnet.q3: If the password is correct, the old session is deleted in the same transaction that creates the new one, which has a freshly generated ID. A malformed or unknown incoming sid is ignored.
sonnet.q4: The cookie carries only the random session ID (32 bytes from a CSPRNG, base64url) and no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At the 12-hour absolute limit since created_at, which is never updated. Activity keeps the 30-minute idle timer restarting but cannot extend the 12 hours.
sonnet.q6: It runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id_hash = $1, clears the cookie (Max-Age=0), and redirects 302 to /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id_hash = sha256(sid), and 0 rows deleted is fine. It then replies 302 /login with the cookie cleared. With no cookie it skips the delete and replies the same way. If the delete fails with a storage error, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: Session state is in the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table keyed by sha256 of the session ID. The instances hold no session state. Either one hashes the sid cookie and queries the same database.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (email, attempted_at default now()), with an index on (email, attempted_at). The window is decided by the database clock: attempted_at compared against now() minus 10 minutes. The doc does not give the exact count query, but all time comparisons use now().
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now() minus 30 minutes (idle limit) and created_at against now() minus 12 hours (absolute limit), using the database clock. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() in the same atomic UPDATE and gets user_id back.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with the login page "Something went wrong. Please try again." The transaction rolls back, no session is created, the cookie is unchanged, and the page does not say whether the credentials were right.
sonnet.q12: A cleanup job that each instance runs every 10 minutes. It deletes sessions with last_seen_at older than 30 minutes or created_at older than 12 hours. The statements are idempotent.
